newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen says Cambodia election on for May 23.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen says Cambodia election on for May 23.

text.p: Cambodia's next election will be on May 23, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted his co-premier in a bloody takeover last week, said in an interview with Voice of America radio.

"My party is like any other party and I hope on May 23, 1998, there will be an election and the election will be free, fair and right," the second prime minister told the radio's Khmer language service.
Hun Sen ousted his coalition government partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on July 6 after two days of fighting in Phnom Penh.
Hun Sen also said he thought relations with the United States were steady despite Washington's decision to suspend aid for 30 days in response to Ranariddh's ouster.
"I think this relationship is not changeable and the suspension of aid for one month I think is not so bad," he said.
Hun Sen and Ranariddh agreed last month that Cambodia's next election would be on May 23, the fifth anniversary of a U.N.-supervised election which Ranariddh's royalist party won.
